label: D1 after a first unrewarded trial while strongly preferring a2, mid-episode
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never GO/D2), almost only when the reward input is 0 (98% of mass), and only while the policy strongly favours a2 (choice logit < -4.4; ~all mass, and good==S2 85%). Has a strong episode-time window: essentially silent before trial ~15 and after trial ~75, so it reads like a slow drift in hidden state. Within these conditions it prefers the first omission after a reward: when the reward two trials back was also 0 it is mostly silent (this term lifts precision from 0.70 to 0.83). Every term is needed: without the choice term precision is 0.21, without the time window 0.47. All variables are observed or computed by the agent (choice is its own logit at D1; ep_trial is elapsed time), so no future variables are used. Activation magnitude was not checked beyond the quartile coverage, which is roughly even (0.9-0.99).

issues: Every factual claim I checked holds. The unit is active only at D1: GO and D2 are 0 of 380619 steps each. 97.6% of mass has in_rew==0. 97.6% of mass has choice < -4.44. good==S2 holds 84.6% of mass. Trials 0-9 have 1 active step and trials 80-99 have 0. Dropping the choice term gives dev precision 0.212 (claimed 0.21). Dropping the episode-time window gives 0.466 (claimed 0.47). Dropping the two-trials-back reward term gives 0.702, against 0.83 with it. The test scores reproduce exactly (P 0.833, R 0.898, F1 0.865, mass recall 0.951).

The label leaves out the main context. Whenever the previous trial's transition is visible in the window, the unit fires only after an a2 choice that went RARELY to S1 and was not rewarded. prev_common==0 holds 81.1% of mass and prev_common==1 holds 0.1%. The other 18.8% is at prev_common==-1, the window's first trial, where the transition can't be seen. prev_action==2 holds 81.1% and prev_action==1 holds 0.1%. On test, adding prev_common==1 to the predicate leaves only 6 steps. So the choice < -4.44 term acts as a proxy: after a2 -> rare S1 -> no reward, a model-based agent strongly prefers repeating a2. The label 'after a first unrewarded trial while strongly preferring a2' is true, but it does not say this is a rare-unrewarded a2 event, which is what the unit means behaviourally.

There is one boundary artifact. Precision at rel -3 is 0.70, against 0.86-0.88 at the other trial positions. On the window's first trial tv('prev_reward', -1) returns -9, so the two-trials-back filter cannot act there. This comes from the window format, not from the unit.

The edges of the episode window are graded, not sharp: within trials 20-24 and 65-69 precision is 0.61, and it is 0.88 inside 25-64. A value band (7.0-7.6) replaces ep_trial less well (F1 0.716 vs 0.792 with the other terms held the same), so the episode-time term is the better one.

The test-split misses show no systematic class. The missed activations hold 4.9% of mass and are mostly small activations just outside the window or the conditions. The false positives are D1 steps after rare-unrewarded trials where the unit stays silent. Adding prev_common != 1 explicitly, or retuning the window bounds, does not change F1 (0.85-0.87 on dev, 0.864 on test). The predicate is close to optimal.
skeptic.revised_label: D1 after an a2 choice that went rarely to S1 and was not rewarded (so the agent strongly prefers repeating a2), when the trial before that was rewarded, mid-episode (trials ~20-70)

final_label: D1 after an a2 choice that went rarely to S1 and was not rewarded (so the agent strongly prefers repeating a2), when the trial before that was rewarded, mid-episode (trials ~20-70)
